true_answer: 26 0. Introduction and Preliminaries 4. { x : x ∈ N ∧− x ∈ N } . Solution . 1. This is the set of all numbers which are 3 less than a natural number (i.e., that if you add 3 to them, you get a natural num- ber). The set could also be written as {− 3 , − 2 , − 1 , 0 , 1 , 2 ,... } (note that 0 is a natural number, so − 3 is in this set because − 3 + 3 | 0 ). 2. This is the set of all natural numbers which are 3 less than a natural number. So here we just have { 0 , 1 , 2 , 3 ... } . 3. This is the set of all integers (positive and negative whole numbers, written Z ).
